regions.region: title, abstract, introduction, and Results and discussion opening
regions.finding: The abstract and introduction state the new CuCl-mediated scope and cite prior carbometallation work; broad claims and cited literature were not duplicated as experiments. The opening prose identifies the paper's preparations of 1a–d, 1e–k, and optically active (S)-1a.

Four distinct reported preparations of propargylic alcohols 1a–d were extracted from the phenylethynylmagnesium bromide/carbonyl sequence, with individual isolated yields; the detailed 1a batch on page 4 was merged into the 1a record.

Seven Sonogashira preparation rows were extracted independently with aryl-halide identity, shared catalysts/solvents/temperature, row time, and isolated yield. The detailed 1e batch on page 4 was merged with entry 1.

unresolved: Scheme 1 gives no batch details for 1b–d beyond structures, sequence, temperature and yields.
Table 1 assigns 1k as 2-CF3C6H4, whereas Table 3 assigns the same label as 3-CF3C6H4; the positional structure remains unresolved.
The paper advertises ESI spectra, but no SI file was provided or explicitly associated.

regions.finding: The Novozym-435 kinetic resolution was treated as one batch with two product-specific isolated yields and ee values; the detailed quantities and purification on page 4 were merged into this record.

Figure 1 supplies NOE-based stereochemical discussion rather than a separate experiment. All nine Table 2 optimization rows were extracted separately, retaining Cu salt/loading, Grignard equivalents, time, both NMR product yields, and recovered 1a as recovery rather than product yield.

regions.region: upper-right Table 3, scheme header, and footnotes
regions.finding: Thirteen substrate/electrophile rows were extracted independently. Shared 1 mmol/CuCl/Grignard/toluene conditions and row-specific times, NMR and isolated yields were retained; entry 4 quench temperature, entry 6 reagent-loading overrides, entry 10 recovery, entry 12 deuterium incorporation, and the NH4Cl definition were applied only to their cited rows.
The low-yield tertiary-alcohol experiment was extracted as a distinct reported batch with 5% NMR product yield and 84% recovered 1d.

unresolved: Most Table 2 and Table 3 rows lack individual workup, purification, and exact batch quantities.
Table 3 assigns 1k as 3-CF3C6H4, conflicting with Table 1's 2-CF3C6H4 assignment.
All depicted structures, regioisomer identities and E/Z assignments remain machine records requiring chemistry review.

regions.finding: Seven iodination scope rows and the separate optically active (S)-1a batch were extracted. Table dashes in entries 3–4 were preserved as undetermined crude NMR yields, not zero; entry 6 retains its room-temperature/heating program.

Seven allylic-bromide trapping rows were extracted independently with Grignard identity, both stage times, allylic-bromide substitution, NMR yield and isolated yield. The detailed E-7a procedure on page 5 was merged into entry 1.

regions.region: middle-right Table 6 and organometallic intermediate drawing
regions.finding: Five Pd-catalyzed coupling rows were extracted. M1 was treated as an in-situ proposed intermediate within the transformation, not an isolated experiment. The detailed 8a procedure and 7% protonolysis byproduct on page 5 were merged into entry 1.
The Pd-catalyzed carbonylation of Z-4a to lactone 9a was extracted as one reported experiment and merged with the detailed page-5 batch.

unresolved: Most scope rows omit exact individual batch quantities, atmosphere, workup and purification.
The M1 drawing is mechanistic/in-situ context and was not assigned an isolated yield or verified structure.

regions.region: left column experimental preparations of 1a and 1e
regions.finding: Exact quantities, staged temperatures/times, workups, purification, product masses and isolated yields were merged into Scheme 1 record 1a and Table 1 entry 1 rather than creating duplicates.

The detailed (S)-1a kinetic-resolution batch supplies reagent/enzyme quantities, 60 °C/23.3 h operation, chromatography, masses, yields and ee values for both products; these were merged into equation 1.

regions.region: right column detailed E-2a and Z-4a preparations
regions.finding: The E-2a batch was merged with Table 3 entry 11 and the Z-4a batch with Table 3 entry 1. Exact starting masses, reagent amounts, atmosphere/temperature operations, workups, chromatography, product masses and isolated yields were retained where represented by the structured fields.

unresolved: Characterization data are identity support and were not converted into separate reactions.
The Z-4a characterization continues on page 5; no new batch begins at that page break.

regions.finding: This is a continuation of the page-4 Z-4a batch and was associated with Table 3 entry 1; it is not a new experiment.
The exact CuCl/Grignard/allyl-bromide quantities, two-stage temperatures, workup, chromatography, product mass and 85% isolated yield were merged into Table 5 entry 1.
The detailed Pd-catalyzed coupling was merged into Table 6 entry 1, retaining exact quantities, 80 °C stage, NMR/isolated yields and the separately reported 7% protonolysis byproduct.
The carbonylation batch was merged with equation 4, retaining Z-4a, Pd(PPh3)4, Et3N, CH3CN, CO pressure text, temperature/time, workup, chromatography, product mass and 67% isolated yield.

unresolved: The 8a protonolysis byproduct is quantified but not fully identified by a separate structure in the supplied pages.
Analytical spectra and elemental analyses support identity but do not independently verify the machine-encoded structures.

regions.region: reference list continuation and page footer
regions.finding: The page contains only bibliographic references 4–12 and closing matter. These are cited prior works, not experiments reported in this paper, so no reaction record was created.

unresolved: Referenced papers were not inspected or expanded; this coverage claim is limited to the supplied paper's page 6.
